# Installed theme: instructions for agents

DOCS_REQUIRED: Name the theme (Theme Name, slug, version from style.css), the site it was
built to carry, and the quickstart id when the site was restored from one.

Read this file before changing anything on this site. It describes the **installed WordPress
site and its theme**, not the Tracy skill that produced them: a maintenance agent may receive
only this webroot and this database.

## Rules

1. This is a WordPress **block theme**. Templates, parts and patterns are files under the theme;
   the site's words are rows in the database. Read docs/architecture.md before touching either.
2. Identify the target before any command: `wp option get siteurl`, `wp theme list --status=active`,
   the webroot path and the process owner. Never assume a localhost stand.
3. Content is edited **through WordPress** — the editor, `wp post update`, or the REST API — as
   block markup. Do not edit the SQL dump, and do not paste a whole page into one `core/html`.
   Read docs/content-model.md for where each kind of text lives.
4. Theme files under `theme.json`, `styles/`, `patterns/`, `templates/`, `parts/`, `assets/css/`
   are **generated by a build** and replaced whole on the next theme update. A hand edit there
   is lost silently. Site-specific overrides go where WordPress keeps them: the Site Editor
   (templates, parts and styles become database rows) or a child theme.
5. A pattern inserted into a page is a **copy**: editing the page changes that page only.
   A synced pattern (`wp_block`) is shared: editing it changes every place that references it.
   Know which one you are holding before you edit.
6. Do not fabricate business facts, legal text, people, prices or images. Demo data stays demo
   until the owner replaces it; a gap is recorded, not filled. Read docs/content-rules.md.
7. Back up before a structural change (`wp db export`, and `wp-content/uploads`). The quickstart
   this site came from is a **baseline**, not a rollback target for an edited site.
   Read docs/checks-and-recovery.md.
8. Report separately: what changed in files, what changed in the database, which checks ran,
   and what could not be verified.

## Read the relevant document before work

| Task | Document |
| --- | --- |
| Folders, what is file vs database, how a request is answered | docs/architecture.md |
| Install the theme, restore the quickstart, identify a site | docs/install.md |
| Where every kind of text lives; adding a section; menus; options | docs/content-model.md |
| Owner decisions, demo data, provenance, known gaps | docs/content-rules.md |
| Tokens, style variations, dark mode, what not to edit by hand | docs/design-system.md |
| Checks by command, backup, restore, theme updates | docs/checks-and-recovery.md |

Source inventory — templates, parts, patterns, variations, presets, blocks, enqueued assets,
and the counts of the seed the site was built with — is in docs/generated/inventory.md. It was
generated from the theme's **files** at build time (`generate-docs.mjs` of the
`tracy-wordpress-theme` skill); it is not a live inventory of this database. Discover current
ids, edited content and installed plugins from the site itself.
